usage: This is the standard morning greeting used every day until around noon. It is universally appropriate for all social situations, from addressing a boss to greeting a street vendor. In Cairo, people often get creative with the responses, wishing mornings of light, jasmine, or roses.

variants.label: casual/friendly
variants.note: A very common, cheerful Egyptian alternative used among friends and colleagues.

variants.label: affectionate
variants.note: Used to show warmth and affection to friends or loved ones.

variants.label: slang/very casual
variants.note: A shortened, slangy version used exclusively with close friends.

examples.transliteration: saba7 el kheir, 3amel eih el naharda?
examples.english: Good morning, how are you today? (to a male)

examples.transliteration: saba7 el kheir, momken fengan ahwa?
examples.english: Good morning, can I have a cup of coffee?
